speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. You mentioned having a low-grade fever, an itchy rash, and joint pain after taking antibiotics; could you tell me which specific antibiotic you were prescribed and for what infection?

speaker: Patient
text: 8-year-old girl. The patient was brought to the emergency department because of a 2-day history of low-grade fever, itchy rash, and generalized joint pain. The rash initially started in the antecubital and popliteal fossae before spreading to the trunk and distal extremities. One week ago, she was diagnosed with acute sinusitis and started on amoxicillin. She has no history of adverse drug reactions, and her immunizations are up to date.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Amoxicillin-Induced Maculopapular Rash (Drug Eruption).

The clinical presentation of fever, an itchy rash starting in flexural areas and spreading to the trunk/extremities, and joint pain following amoxicillin use for sinusitis is classic for a delayed hypersensitivity reaction. I am confident in this diagnosis based on the temporal relationship and morphology described, so no further questions or tests are required.
